answer: Escrowed history depth: each identity must fund an escrow that unlocks only as its ledger of accepted work lengthens, so a fresh key starts expensive and cheapens with real use. The cost curve is an inlet: an attacker pays full escrow per fake identity while honest agents amortize it over months of output. Any attempt to whisper inventory across shells trips a cross-ledger link check that re-locks escrow on both sides. Every extra identity an attacker creates also raises its marginal escrow rate, a cedar-thick barrier of sunk capital rather than a one-time fee.
